Fewer than `n` if the spine is shorter. NOTE: a bounded window collapses\n126\t        a RAPID (recent) replay flood, but does NOT bound AGGREGATE replay bloat — a rotated pool of\n127\t        distinct bodies larger than the window each ages out and re-records. Only pair `tail()`-based\n128\t        dedup with a record-time freshness gate (or an independent bound); do not rely on it alone to\n129\t        close a bloat sink.\"\"\"\n130\t        if n <= 0 or not self.path.exists():\n131\t            return []\n132\t        with self.path.open(\"rb\") as f:\n133\t            f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)\n134\t            pos = f.tell()\n135\t            buf = b\"\"\n136\t            while pos > 0 and buf.count(b\"\\n\") <= n:\n137\t                step = min(65536, pos)\n138\t                pos -= step\n139\t                f.seek(pos)\n140\t                buf = f.read(step) + buf\n141\t        recs: list[SpineRecord] = []\n142\t        for ln in [x for x in buf.split(b\"\\n\") if x.strip()][-n:]:\n143\t            try:\n144\t                recs.append(SpineRecord.from_dict(json.loads(ln)))\n145\t            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):\n146\t                continue\n147\t        return recs\n148\t\n149\t    @property\n150\t    def next_seq(self) -> int:\n151\t        return (self._last.seq + 1) if self._last else 0\n152\t\n153\t    def count(self) -> int:\n154\t        return sum(1 for _ in self.iter_records())\n155\t\n156\t    # --- integrity ----------------------------------------------------------------\n157\t    def entries(self) -> list[ChainEntry]:\n158\t        return [\n159\t            ChainEntry(seq=r.seq, prev_hash=r.prev_hash, cert_digest=r.cert_digest, entry_hash=r.entry_hash)\n160\t            for r in self.iter_records()\n161\t        ]\n162\t\n163\t    def verify(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n164\t        \"\"\"Two-layer UNKEYED integrity: (1) BINDING — each record's payload still hashes to its\n165\t        stored cert_digest (catches silent payload edits); (2) CHAIN — the entries link cleanly\n166\t        (catches delete/reorder/entry tamper). This proves internal CONSISTENCY, not authenticity:\n167\t        a naive payload edit fails (1), and a mid-chain digest edit cascades an entry_hash/prev_hash\n168\t        break caught by (2) — BUT a writer who recomputes cert_digest+entry_hash for the tip (no\n169\t        successor to cascade into) or forward-cascades a fork produces a self-consistent chain that\n170\t        passes here. Resistance to a recompute-capable writer is the owner-SIGNED head's job\n171\t        (`checkpoint.verify_checkpoint`, Ed25519 + monotonic last_seq). Use this for corruption/\n172\t        naive-tamper detection; use the signed head for tamper-EVIDENCE.\"\"\"\n173\t        entries: list[ChainEntry] = []\n174\t        for r in self.iter_records():\n175\t            content = {\n176\t                \"scope\": r.scope, \"kind\": r.kind, \"source\": r.source, \"actor\": r.actor,\n177\t                \"payload\": r.payload, \"parent_id\": r.parent_id, \"supersedes_id\": r.supersedes_id,\n178\t            }\n179\t            if digest_payload(content) != r.cert_digest:\n180\t                return False, f\"binding break at seq {r.seq}: payload does not match cert_digest (record tampered)\"\n181\t            entries.append(ChainEntry(seq=r.seq, prev_hash=r.prev_hash, cert_digest=r.cert_digest, entry_hash=r.entry_hash))\n182\t        return verify_chain(entries)\n183\t\n184\t    def _read_last_entry(self) -> ChainEntry | None:\n185\t        line = _last_nonempty_line(self.path) if self.path.exists() else None\n186\t        if not line:\n187\t            return None\n188\t        d = json.loads(line)\n189\t        return ChainEntry(seq=d[\"seq\"], prev_hash=d[\"prev_hash\"], cert_digest=d[\"cert_digest\"], entry_hash=d[\"entry_hash\"])\n190\t"}]},"uuid":"c68b75d9-99f0-4916-a954-ca9be7b796e2","timestamp":"2026-07-19T09:11:34.899Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d63a6958-6cdb-46b4-9bb7-b3d278736fdb","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"0506b9dd-41bd-4d54-9e09-dfa2512f225b","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"3f8d7a84-2083-490c-adb3-be5a0da7c099","agentId":"a3b7991d5205d8298","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XqmY4KVB93dcvz82d18Xez","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"SpineTailer (Phase 7, P0.2) — a live tail over the append-only, poll-only spine with an HONEST,\n2\ttwo-layer integrity model (red-pen-hardened: unkeyed hashes alone cannot resist a writer who can\n3\trecompute them):\n4\t\n5\t  • `integrity_ok` (CHEAP, per-poll, unkeyed) — per-record binding+derivation (`verify_record`) plus\n6\t    cross-record LINKAGE (this record's `prev_hash` == the last emitted `entry_hash`). This catches\n7\t    ACCIDENTAL corruption, a naive stale-field tamper, a deletion/reorder/gap. It does NOT resist a\n8\t    file-writer who recomputes cert_digest+entry_hash (a tip tamper or a forward-cascaded fork stays\n9\t    internally consistent) — so it is necessary but not sufficient, and is never presented as proof\n10\t    of authenticity on its own.\n11\t\n12\t  • `anchored` (KEYED, via `check_anchor`) — the owner-SIGNED head (`checkpoint.classify_head` /\n13\t    `verify_head`, Ed25519 1-of-1 trust root, monotonic `last_seq`) notarizes the prefix\n14\t    [0 .. signed_last_seq]. A recompute-fork or truncation AT OR BELOW the signed head is\n15\t    unforgeable without the owner key and is caught here; a monotonic high-water catches a rollback\n16\t    of even the un-notarized tail. Records with seq > signed_last_seq are the FRESH, not-yet-keyed\n17\t    tail — emitted `anchored=False` (well-formed but not tamper-proof), keyed at the next `sigil sign`.\n18\t\n19\tA consumer (UI/mobile) shows `integrity_ok=False` as \"integrity broken\", and treats only\n20\t`anchored=True` records as owner-notarized truth; the un-notarized tail is labelled as such, never\n21\tdressed up as proven. One primitive, two consumers — the UI SSE feed and the mobile push notifier —\n22\tboth drive `poll()` on a tick and fan events out via `Broadcaster`.\"\"\"\n23\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n24\t\n25\tfrom collections import deque\n26\tfrom typing import Optional\n27\t\n28\tfrom ..config import HEAD_PATH\n29\tfrom ..reuse import SignedChainHead\n30\tfrom ..reuse.chain import _GENESIS_PREV\n31\tfrom .checkpoint import classify_head, trust_root\n32\tfrom .store import SpineStore\n33\tfrom .verify import verify_record\n34\t\n35\t\n36\tdef _shape(record, *, integrity_ok: bool, integrity_reason: str, anchored: bool) -> dict:\n37\t    \"\"\"The cited atom shape emitted to consumers. `integrity_ok` = unkeyed well-formedness;\n38\t    `anchored` = covered by the owner-signed head (keyed). `text` is best-effort, never fabricated.\"\"\"\n39\t    return {\n40\t        \"seq\": record.seq, \"kind\": record.kind, \"source\": record.source, \"actor\": record.actor,\n41\t        \"ts\": record.ts, \"entry_hash\": record.entry_hash, \"text\": record.text(),\n42\t        \"integrity_ok\": integrity_ok, \"integrity_reason\": integrity_reason, \"anchored\": anchored,\n43\t    }\n44\t\n45\t\n46\tclass SpineTailer:\n47\t    def __init__(self, store: Optional[SpineStore] = None, *, since_seq: int = -1,\n48\t                 signed_head: Optional[SignedChainHead] = None, tr=None):\n49\t        \"\"\"Emit records with seq > `since_seq`. `signed_head`/`tr` may be injected (tests); otherwise\n50\t        the owner-signed head is loaded from `HEAD_PATH` + the persisted trust root.\"\"\"\n51\t        self.store = store or SpineStore()\n52\t        self.cursor = since_seq\n53\t        if since_seq < 0:\n54\t            self._last_hash = _GENESIS_PREV\n55\t        else:\n56\t            anchor = self.store.get(since_seq)\n57\t            self._last_hash = anchor.entry_hash if anchor else _GENESIS_PREV\n58\t        self._injected_head = signed_head\n59\t        self._injected_tr = tr\n60\t        self._high_water = -1                           # monotonic anti-rollback water mark\n61\t        self._signed_last_seq = -1\n62\t        self.check_anchor()                             # establish the initial keyed anchor (reads disk)\n63\t\n64\t    def poll(self) -> list[dict]:\n65\t        \"\"\"Newly-appended records (seq > cursor), each with the cheap `integrity_ok` verdict and the\n66\t        `anchored` (keyed) flag from the last `check_anchor`. On an integrity failure the event is\n67\t        emitted flagged (not dropped); the cursor still advances so the feed never re-emits or stalls.\"\"\"\n68\t        out: list[dict] = []\n69\t        for r in self.store.iter_records(since_seq=self.cursor):\n70\t            atom_ok, reason = verify_record(r)\n71\t            if r.prev_hash != self._last_hash:\n72\t                ok = False\n73\t                reason = f\"linkage break at seq {r.seq}: prev_hash != last emitted entry_hash (rewind/fork/gap)\"\n74\t            else:\n75\t                ok = atom_ok\n76\t            out.append(_shape(r, integrity_ok=ok, integrity_reason=reason,\n77\t                              anchored=(r.seq <= self._signed_last_seq)))\n78\t            self.cursor = r.seq\n79\t            self._last_hash = r.entry_hash\n80\t        return out\n81\t\n82\t    def check_anchor(self) -> dict:\n83\t        \"\"\"The KEYED verdict. Verify the owner-signed head over the current chain (unforgeable without\n84\t        the owner key): a recompute-fork or truncation at/below the signed head → `anchor_ok=False`;\n85\t        a monotonic high-water rollback of even the un-notarized tail → `rollback` set. Updates\n86\t        `signed_last_seq` so `poll()` can flag records beyond it as the un-notarized tail.\"\"\"\n87\t        entries = self.store.entries()                  # FRESH read from disk (not the cached head)\n88\t        head_seq = entries[-1].seq if entries else -1\n89\t        rollback = None\n90\t        if head_seq < self._high_water:\n91\t            rollback = f\"ROLLBACK: on-disk head seq {head_seq} < monotonic high-water {self._high_water}\"\n92\t        else:\n93\t            self._high_water = head_seq\n94\t        head, tr = self._resolve_head()\n95\t        if head is None:\n96\t            self._signed_last_seq = -1\n97\t            return {\"anchor_ok\": False, \"signed_last_seq\": -1, \"rollback\": rollback,\n98\t                    \"reason\": \"no signed checkpoint — the live tail is well-formed but UN-NOTARIZED \"\n99\t                              \"(run `sigil sign` to anchor)\"}\n100\t        try:\n101\t            ok, reason = classify_head(head, entries, tr)\n102\t        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — a malformed head must FAIL closed, never crash the feed\n103\t            self._signed_last_seq = -1\n104\t            return {\"anchor_ok\": False, \"signed_last_seq\": -1, \"rollback\": rollback,\n105\t                    \"reason\": f\"anchor unverifiable ({e})\"}\n106\t        self._signed_last_seq = head.last_seq if ok else -1\n107\t        return {\"anchor_ok\": ok and rollback is None, \"signed_last_seq\": self._signed_last_seq,\n108\t                \"rollback\": rollback, \"reason\": reason}\n109\t\n110\t    def _resolve_head(self):\n111\t        if self._injected_head is not None:\n112\t            return self._injected_head, self._injected_tr\n113\t        try:\n114\t            if not HEAD_PATH.exists():\n115\t                return None, None\n116\t            head = SignedChainHead.model_validate_json(HEAD_PATH.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n117\t            return head, trust_root()\n118\t        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — no/broken head → unkeyed live tail (honest, fail-closed)\n119\t            return None, None\n120\t\n121\t\n122\tclass Broadcaster:\n123\t    \"\"\"Fan-out of tail events to N subscribers with bounded per-subscriber queues. On overflow the\n124\t    oldest events are dropped and the subscriber is marked `lagged` so it resyncs from the cursor\n125\t    (never a fabricated 'you saw everything').\"\"\"\n126\t    def __init__(self, maxlen: int = 512):\n127\t        self.maxlen = maxlen\n128\t        self._subs: dict[int, deque] = {}\n129\t        self._lagged: dict[int, bool] = {}\n130\t        self._next_id = 0\n131\t\n132\t    def subscribe(self) -> int:\n133\t        sid = self._next_id\n134\t        self._next_id += 1\n135\t        self._subs[sid] = deque(maxlen=self.maxlen)\n136\t        self._lagged[sid] = False\n137\t        return sid\n138\t\n139\t    def unsubscribe(self, sid: int) -> None:\n140\t        self._subs.pop(sid, None)\n141\t        self._lagged.pop(sid, None)\n142\t\n143\t    def publish(self, events: list[dict]) -> None:\n144\t        for sid, q in self._subs.items():\n145\t            for ev in events:\n146\t                if len(q) == self.maxlen:        # would drop the oldest → the subscriber lagged\n147\t                    self._lagged[sid] = True\n148\t                q.append(ev)\n149\t\n150\t    def drain(self, sid: int) -> tuple[list[dict], bool]:\n151\t        \"\"\"Return (events, lagged) and clear both. `lagged=True` tells the consumer to resync.\"\"\"\n152\t        q = self._subs.get(sid)\n153\t        if q is None:\n154\t            return [], False\n155\t        events = list(q)\n156\t        q.clear()\n157\t        lagged = self._lagged.get(sid, False)\n158\t        self._lagged[sid] = False\n159\t        return events, lagged\n160\t"}]},"uuid":"882dde58-4a27-424f-b236-d146216e7e9a","timestamp":"2026-07-19T09:11:35.323Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0506b9dd-41bd-4d54-9e09-dfa2512f225b","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"e67a2d51-92a3-4051-b8ea-d109c7fb6ac8","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"3f8d7a84-2083-490c-adb3-be5a0da7c099","agentId":"a3b7991d5205d8298","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EMUtFLPxRgwNbuGFtEipxp","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Daily signed checkpoint of the spine head (SIGIL §6.3.6, WARDEN anchor).\n2\t\n3\tGenerates + persists a solo-owner Ed25519 keypair once (1-of-1 trust root), then signs\n4\tthe chain head so the whole spine is anchored: rewriting history would require forging\n5\tthe owner signature, and a shrunk/back-dated head is caught by the monotonic last_seq.\n6\t\n7\tNote: for a personal, single-owner, local-first system the owner's signing key lives\n8\tlocally (0600) — a deliberate simplification of the framework's \"keys never on the\n9\truntime host\" rule, appropriate to this threat model (§1.3). A hardware co-signer can be\n10\tadded later by raising the trust-root threshold.\n11\t\"\"\"\n12\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n13\t\n14\timport os\n15\t\n16\tfrom ..config import HEAD_PATH, KEYS_DIR, OWNER_KEY_ID, SCOPE\n17\tfrom ..reuse import (\n18\t    AuthorizerKey,\n19\t    SignedChainHead,\n20\t    TrustRoot,\n21\t    generate_keypair,\n22\t    sign_head,\n23\t    verify_head,\n24\t)\n25\tfrom .store import SpineStore\n26\t\n27\t_PRIV = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.priv\"\n28\t_PUB = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.pub\"\n29\t\n30\t\n31\tdef _owner_keys() -> tuple[str, str]:\n32\t    if not _PRIV.exists():\n33\t        KEYS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n34\t        kp = generate_keypair()\n35\t        _PRIV.write_text(kp.private_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n36\t        os.chmod(_PRIV, 0o600)\n37\t        _PUB.write_text(kp.public_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n38\t    return _PRIV.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip(), _PUB.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip()\n39\t\n40\t\n41\tdef trust_root() -> TrustRoot:\n42\t    _, pub = _owner_keys()\n43\t    return TrustRoot(threshold=1, authorizers=[\n44\t        AuthorizerKey(key_id=OWNER_KEY_ID, name=\"owner\", public_key_b64=pub)])\n45\t\n46\t\n47\tdef checkpoint(store: SpineStore | None = None) -> SignedChainHead:\n48\t    store = store or SpineStore()\n49\t    priv, _ = _owner_keys()\n50\t    head = sign_head(store.entries(), engagement_slug=SCOPE, signers=[(OWNER_KEY_ID, priv)])\n51\t    HEAD_PATH.write_text(head.model_dump_json(), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n52\t    return head\n53\t\n54\t\n55\tdef classify_head(head: SignedChainHead, entries: list, tr: TrustRoot) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n56\t    \"\"\"Pure head/chain classification (no globals — testable in isolation). Distinguishes\n57\t    three cases honestly: a shrunk chain (truncation) or a mismatching prefix (history\n58\t    rewrite) are TAMPERING; a chain that merely grew past the anchor is benign — stale.\n59\t    \"\"\"\n60\t    n, signed_n = len(entries), head.entry_count\n61\t    if n < signed_n:\n62\t        return False, f\"TAMPERING: chain has {n} records but the signed head anchors {signed_n} (truncated/rolled back)\"\n63\t    # verify the head against exactly the prefix it signed; append-only ⇒ the prefix is byte-identical.\n64\t    ok, msg = verify_head(head, entries[:signed_n], tr)\n65\t    if not ok:\n66\t        return False, f\"TAMPERING: history rewritten at or below the signed head — {msg}\"\n67\t    if n > signed_n:\n68\t        return True, f\"anchors {signed_n} records; {n - signed_n} appended since — run `sigil sign` to re-anchor\"\n69\t    return True, f\"anchors all {signed_n} records (current)\"\n70\t\n71\t\n72\tdef verify_checkpoint(store: SpineStore | None = None) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n73\t    store = store or SpineStore()\n74\t    if not HEAD_PATH.exists():\n75\t        return False, \"no signed head — run `sigil sign` to anchor the spine\"\n76\t    head = SignedChainHead.model_validate_json(HEAD_PATH.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n77\t    return classify_head(head, store.entries(), trust_root())\n78\t"}]},"uuid":"e0b34f85-a5e3-491f-b714-7bfb239a02d3","timestamp":"2026-07-19T09:11:35.826Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"e67a2d51-92a3-4051-b8ea-d109c7fb6ac8","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"ee103730-3164-4531-9e36-d9c1629b3025","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"3f8d7a84-2083-490c-adb3-be5a0da7c099","agentId":"a3b7991d5205d8298","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SMNqZFKcK4tHpp6tp7PAMX","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"verify_record (Phase 7, P0.2) — the single \"prove-this-atom\" helper reused by the live tail,\n2\tthe UI `/api/record` endpoint, and the mobile daemon, so \"serve-the-quote / prove-don't-guess\" is\n3\tONE implementation, not three. It performs the two per-atom checks the store's `verify()` does for\n4\tthe whole log, on a single record:\n5\t\n6\t  1. BINDING — the record's content still hashes to its stored `cert_digest` (catches a silent\n7\t     payload edit).\n8\t  2. DERIVATION — `entry_hash` is correctly derived from (seq, prev_hash, cert_digest) (catches an\n9\t     entry-field tamper).\n10\t\n11\tCross-record LINKAGE (prev_hash == the predecessor's entry_hash) needs the predecessor and is done\n12\tby `SpineTailer` as records stream. State is append-only on the spine.\n3\t\n4\tASYMMETRIC AUTHENTICATION (Phase 6 red-pen RP-2): halting is always the safe direction, so ANY\n5\tengage event halts (a nuisance forged-engage is at worst a fail-safe DoS). UN-halting is the\n6\tdangerous direction, so a RELEASE is honored ONLY if it is signed by the owner key and verifies\n7\tagainst the trusted pubkey — a forged release can never revive a halted mesh. Read fresh per decision\n8\tso a release (or engage) takes effect immediately.\"\"\"\n9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n10\t\n11\tfrom typing import Optional\n12\t\n13\tfrom .authn import signed_payload, verify_signed\n14\tfrom .identity import owner_keypair, owner_pubkey\n15\t\n16\tSIGNAL = \"governor.killswitch\"\n17\t_CORE = (\"signal\", \"state\")\n18\t\n19\t\n20\tclass KillSwitch:\n21\t    def __init__(self, store, *, owner_key=None, trusted_pubkey: Optional[str] = None):\n22\t        self.store = store\n23\t        self.owner_key = owner_key if owner_key is not None else owner_keypair()\n24\t        self.trusted_pubkey = trusted_pubkey if trusted_pubkey is not None else owner_pubkey()\n25\t\n26\t    def engage(self, *, by: str = \"owner\", reason: str = \"\") -> int:\n27\t        core = {\"signal\": SIGNAL, \"state\": \"engaged\"}\n28\t        payload = {**signed_payload(core, self.owner_key), \"by\": by, \"reason\": reason,\n29\t                   \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"}\n30\t        return self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"governor\", actor=\"WARDEN\", payload=payload)\n31\t\n32\t    def release(self, *, by: str = \"owner\", reason: str = \"\") -> int:\n33\t        core = {\"signal\": SIGNAL, \"state\": \"released\"}\n34\t        payload = {**signed_payload(core, self.owner_key), \"by\": by, \"reason\": reason,\n35\t                   \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"}\n36\t        return self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"governor\", actor=\"WARDEN\", payload=payload)\n37\t\n38\t    def is_engaged(self) -> bool:\n39\t        engaged = False\n40\t        for r in self.store.iter_records():\n41\t            p = r.payload\n42\t            if p.get(\"signal\") != SIGNAL:\n43\t                continue\n44\t            state = p.get(\"state\")\n45\t            if state == \"engaged\":\n46\t                engaged = True                      # honor ANY engage — halting is fail-safe\n47\t            elif state == \"released\" and verify_signed(p, _CORE, self.trusted_pubkey):\n48\t                engaged = False                     # only an OWNER-SIGNED release un-halts (fail-closed)\n49\t        return engaged\n50\t"}]},"uuid":"434c8762-e4d8-44e0-896e-33ef425749c6","timestamp":"2026-07-19T09:11:36.452Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"3da07c75-3de6-471b-be2f-8f5c98e61a0d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"62a0cf73-a584-4745-9f11-0e03596f9df2","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"3f8d7a84-2083-490c-adb3-be5a0da7c099","agentId":"a3b7991d5205d8298","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01PwEjFLs2Bs6BfJKYBeRAmX","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"The episodic spine record — one immutable event, source of truth (SIGIL §6.1).\"\"\"\n2\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n3\t\n4\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n5\tfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\n6\tfrom typing import Any\n7\t\n8\t# event kinds (superset of the CRUCIBLE blackboard EventKind, extended for SIGIL sources)\n9\tKINDS = frozenset({\n10\t    \"message\", \"tool_call\", \"tool_result\", \"decision\", \"commitment\",\n11\t    \"commit\", \"document\", \"brief\", \"refusal\", \"email\", \"session\",\n12\t    \"entity\", \"contradiction\",  # promoted by the ARCHIVIST consolidation pass (§6.3)\n13\t    \"warden_checkpoint\",        # WARDEN (Phase 1) cross-anchors its action-log head here (anti-rollback)\n14\t    \"event\", \"finding\", \"interaction\", \"draft\",  # the agent mesh (Phase 3, §4): SENTINEL/BASTION/ENVOY\n15\t    \"report\", \"pr\",             # Phase 4: SCHOLAR sourced research reports, ARTIFICER PR proposals\n16\t    \"web_page\", \"operation\",    # Phase 7/8: SCRIBE fetched-page provenance; OPERATOR plan/execute records\n17\t})\n18\t\n19\t\n20\tdef now_iso() -> str:\n21\t    \"\"\"Informational wallclock timestamp. NOT part of the content digest (replay-stable).\"\"\"\n22\t    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()\n23\t\n24\t\n25\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n26\tclass SpineRecord:\n27\t    \"\"\"One line of the spine. `cert_digest`/`prev_hash`/`entry_hash` are the chain fields;\n28\t    everything above `ts` is the digested content (ts is informational, excluded from the digest).\"\"\"\n29\t    seq: int\n30\t    scope: str\n31\t    kind: str\n32\t    source: str            # \"claude-code\" | \"git\" | \"doc\" | ...\n33\t    actor: str             # \"user\" | \"assistant\" | session id | commit author | ...\n34\t    payload: dict[str, Any]\n35\t    parent_id: int | None\n36\t    supersedes_id: int | None\n37\t    ts: str\n38\t    cert_digest: str\n39\t    prev_hash: str\n40\t    entry_hash: str\n41\t\n42\t    @classmethod\n43\t    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> \"SpineRecord\":\n44\t        return cls(\n45\t            seq=d[\"seq\"], scope=d[\"scope\"], kind=d[\"kind\"], source=d[\"source\"],\n46\t            actor=d[\"actor\"], payload=d.get(\"payload\") or {},\n47\t            parent_id=d.get(\"parent_id\"), supersedes_id=d.get(\"supersedes_id\"),\n48\t            ts=d.get(\"ts\", \"\"), cert_digest=d[\"cert_digest\"],\n49\t            prev_hash=d[\"prev_hash\"], entry_hash=d[\"entry_hash\"],\n50\t        )\n51\t\n52\t    def text(self) -> str:\n53\t        \"\"\"Best-effort human/searchable text of the record (for embedding + display).\"\"\"\n54\t        p = self.payload or {}\n55\t        for key in (\"text\", \"content\", \"message\", \"summary\", \"body\", \"title\"):\n56\t            v = p.get(key)\n57\t            if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip():\n58\t                return v\n59\t        # tool records / structured payloads: compact JSON fallback\n60\t        import json\n61\t        return json.dumps(p, ensure_ascii=False)[:4000]\n62\t"}]},"uuid":"91da2f44-b8c8-4ec8-aaa0-185403b829f5","timestamp":"2026-07-19T09:11:41.639Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"62a0cf73-a584-4745-9f11-0e03596f9df2","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

Run: ~/.sigil/venv/bin/python tests/test_integrity.py\"\"\"\n2\timport json\n3\timport tempfile\n4\t\n5\tfrom sigil import reuse\n6\tfrom sigil.spine.store import SpineStore\n7\t\n8\t\n9\tdef _fresh(n=5):\n10\t    p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=\".jsonl\")\n11\t    s = SpineStore(p)\n12\t    for i in range(n):\n13\t        s.append(kind=\"message\", source=\"t\", actor=\"u\", payload={\"text\": f\"event {i}\"})\n14\t    return p, s\n15\t\n16\t\n17\tdef test_tail_returns_the_last_n_records():   # tightening #2 (bounded-window dedup)\n18\t    p, _ = _fresh(10)                          # 10 records, seq 0..9\n19\t    s = SpineStore(p)\n20\t    assert [r.seq for r in s.tail(3)] == [7, 8, 9], \"tail(3) = the last three records, in order\"\n21\t    assert len(s.tail(100)) == 10, \"tail(n > len) returns all\"\n22\t    assert s.tail(0) == [], \"tail(0) is empty\"\n23\t\n24\t\n25\tdef test_concurrent_appends_do_not_fork_the_chain():   # Phase 9 sweep HIGH-2 (threaded bridge server exposes it)\n26\t    import threading\n27\t    p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=\".jsonl\")\n28\t    SpineStore(p).append(kind=\"event\", source=\"t\", actor=\"u\", payload={\"seed\": True})\n29\t    barrier = threading.Barrier(8)\n30\t\n31\t    def w(i):\n32\t        barrier.wait()\n33\t        SpineStore(p).append(kind=\"event\", source=\"t\", actor=\"u\", payload={\"i\": i})   # FRESH instance per thread\n34\t\n35\t    threads = [threading.Thread(target=w, args=(i,)) for i in range(8)]\n36\t    for t in threads:\n37\t        t.start()\n38\t    for t in threads:\n39\t        t.join()\n40\t    seqs = [r.seq for r in SpineStore(p).iter_records()]\n41\t    assert len(seqs) == len(set(seqs)) == 9, f\"8 concurrent appends produce distinct seqs (no fork): {sorted(seqs)}\"\n42\t    ok, reason = SpineStore(p).verify()\n43\t    assert ok, f\"the hash chain stays intact after concurrent appends: {reason}\"\n44\t\n45\t\n46\tdef test_clean_verifies():\n47\t    _, s = _fresh()\n48\t    ok, _ = s.verify()\n49\t    assert ok, \"clean spine must verify\"\n50\t\n51\t\n52\tdef test_payload_tamper_caught():\n53\t    p, _ = _fresh()\n54\t    lines = open(p).read().splitlines()\n55\t    o = json.loads(lines[1]); o[\"payload\"] = {\"text\": \"TAMPERED\"}; lines[1] = json.dumps(o)\n56\t    open(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(lines) + \"\\n\")\n57\t    ok, msg = SpineStore(p).verify()\n58\t    assert not ok and \"binding break\" in msg, f\"payload tamper must fail binding: {msg}\"\n59\t\n60\t\n61\tdef test_delete_caught():\n62\t    p, _ = _fresh()\n63\t    lines = open(p).read().splitlines(); del lines[2]\n64\t    open(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(lines) + \"\\n\")\n65\t    ok, msg = SpineStore(p).verify()\n66\t    assert not ok and \"chain break\" in msg, f\"delete must fail chain: {msg}\"\n67\t\n68\t\n69\tdef test_reopen_seek_from_end():\n70\t    p, _ = _fresh(3)\n71\t    s2 = SpineStore(p)\n72\t    seq = s2.append(kind=\"message\", source=\"t\", actor=\"u\", payload={\"text\": \"reopened\"})\n73\t    assert seq == 3 and s2.verify()[0], \"reopen must continue the chain\"\n74\t\n75\t\n76\tdef test_digest_is_wallclock_free():\n77\t    # same content, different ts → identical cert_digest (replay-stable)\n78\t    c = {\"scope\": \"sigil\", \"kind\": \"message\", \"source\": \"t\", \"actor\": \"u\",\n79\t         \"payload\": {\"text\": \"x\"}, \"parent_id\": None, \"supersedes_id\": None}\n80\t    assert reuse.digest_payload(c) == reuse.digest_payload(dict(c)), \"digest must ignore ts\"\n81\t\n82\t\n83\tdef test_sign_and_verify_head():\n84\t    _, s = _fresh(4)\n85\t    kp = reuse.generate_keypair()\n86\t    tr = reuse.TrustRoot(threshold=1, authorizers=[\n87\t        reuse.AuthorizerKey(key_id=\"owner\", name=\"owner\", public_key_b64=kp.public_key_b64)])\n88\t    head = reuse.sign_head(s.entries(), engagement_slug=\"sigil\", signers=[(\"owner\", kp.private_key_b64)])\n89\t    ok, msg = reuse.verify_head(head, s.entries(), tr)\n90\t    assert ok, f\"signed head must verify: {msg}\"\n91\t\n92\t\n93\tdef _head_over(store, n):\n94\t    \"\"\"Sign a head over the first `n` entries; return (head, trust_root).\"\"\"\n95\t    kp = reuse.generate_keypair()\n96\t    tr = reuse.TrustRoot(threshold=1, authorizers=[\n97\t        reuse.AuthorizerKey(key_id=\"owner\", name=\"owner\", public_key_b64=kp.public_key_b64)])\n98\t    head = reuse.sign_head(store.entries()[:n], engagement_slug=\"sigil\",\n99\t                           signers=[(\"owner\", kp.private_key_b64)])\n100\t    return head, tr\n101\t\n102\t\n103\tdef test_growth_is_benign_not_tampering():\n104\t    from sigil.spine.checkpoint import classify_head\n105\t    _, s = _fresh(4)\n106\t    head, tr = _head_over(s, 4)\n107\t    s.append(kind=\"message\", source=\"t\", actor=\"u\", payload={\"text\": \"later\"})  # grow past anchor\n108\t    ok, msg = classify_head(head, s.entries(), tr)\n109\t    assert ok and \"appended\" in msg and \"TAMPERING\" not in msg, f\"growth must be benign: {msg}\"\n110\t\n111\t\n112\tdef test_truncation_below_head_is_tampering():\n113\t    from sigil.spine.checkpoint import classify_head\n114\t    _, s = _fresh(5)\n115\t    head, tr = _head_over(s, 5)\n116\t    ok, msg = classify_head(head, s.entries()[:3], tr)  # Plus self-audit (incl.\n4\tdenials), the read-only dashboard, and the SSRF gate with IP pinning.\n5\tRun: ~/.sigil/venv/bin/python tests/test_hardening.py\n6\t\n7\tThe acceptance bar is \"zero unauthorized A2/A3 in the audit log\": these prove the gate is airtight and\n8\tgovernance events are owner-signed, so an A2-auto log line PROVES a real owner promotion.\"\"\"\n9\timport tempfile\n10\tfrom pathlib import Path\n11\t\n12\tfrom sigil.agents.base import Agent, Proposal, Tier\n13\tfrom sigil.governor import BudgetCaps, Governor, KillSwitch, PromotionPolicy\n14\tfrom sigil.governor.authn import signed_payload\n15\tfrom sigil.reuse import generate_keypair\n16\tfrom sigil.spine.store import SpineStore\n17\t\n18\tOWNER = generate_keypair()                 # the established owner identity for these tests\n19\tOWNER_PUB = OWNER.public_key_b64\n20\t\n21\t\n22\tdef _store():\n23\t    return SpineStore(tempfile.mktemp(suffix=\".jsonl\"))\n24\t\n25\t\n26\tdef _gov(store, *, caps=None):\n27\t    return Governor(store, caps=caps, owner_key=OWNER, trusted_pubkey=OWNER_PUB)\n28\t\n29\t\n30\tclass _Emitter(Agent):\n31\t    name = \"TESTER\"\n32\t    ceiling = Tier.A2\n33\t\n34\t    def __init__(self, store, *, caps=None):\n35\t        super().__init__(store, governor=_gov(store, caps=caps))\n36\t\n37\t    def run(self, tier, kind=\"event\"):\n38\t        return self._dispatch([Proposal(kind, {\"subject\": \"x\"}, tier)])\n39\t\n40\t\n41\t# ---- kill switch: any engage halts; only a SIGNED release restores -------------------------------\n42\tdef test_killswitch_halts_and_only_signed_release_restores():\n43\t    s = _store()\n44\t    KillSwitch(s, owner_key=OWNER).engage(reason=\"drill\")\n45\t    t = _Emitter(s)\n46\t    assert t.run(Tier.A0).applied, \"A0 observe stays alive under the kill switch\"\n47\t    assert not t.run(Tier.A1).applied, \"A1 agent action is halted\"\n48\t    # grant signed by a NON-owner key also grants nothing\n97\t    attacker = generate_keypair()\n98\t    s.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"governor\", actor=\"WARDEN\",\n99\t             payload=signed_payload({\"signal\": \"governor.promotion\", \"state\": \"granted\",\n100\t                                     \"agent\": \"TESTER\", \"scope\": \"draft\"}, attacker))\n101\t    assert t.run(Tier.A2, kind=\"draft\").queued, \"a non-owner-signed grant auto-approves nothing\"\n102\t\n103\t\n104\tdef test_envoy_has_no_promotion_path():\n105\t    s = _store()\n106\t    assert PromotionPolicy(s, owner_key=OWNER).grant(\"ENVOY\", \"*\") is None, \"promoting ENVOY is refused\"\n107\t    # wrong signing key\n177\t    try:\n178\t        q.approve(tgt)\n179\t        assert False, \"an attacker key must not approve against the owner's trusted key\"\n180\t    except ApprovalError:\n181\t        pass\n182\t\n183\t\n184\t# ---- dashboard (read-only) -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n185\tdef test_dashboard_is_read_only_and_counts_only_real_actions():\n186\t    from sigil.dashboard import render_dashboard, snapshot\n187\t    s = _store()\n188\t    t = _Emitter(s)\n189\t    t.run(Tier.A1)\n190\t    KillSwitch(s, owner_key=OWNER).engage()\n191\t    t.run(Tier.A2, kind=\"draft\")     # DENIED (kill engaged) → must NOT inflate budget usage\n192\t    before = s.count()\n193\t    snap = snapshot(s)\n194\t    assert s.count() == before, \"the dashboard writes NOTHING to the spine\"\n195\t    assert snap[\"kill_switch\"] == \"ENGAGED\"\n196\t    assert snap[\"budget_today\"].get(\"TESTER\", {}).get(\"actions\") == 1, \"denied attempts don't count as actions\"\n197\t    assert \"Kill switch\" in render_dashboard(snap)\n198\t\n199\t\n200\t# ---- SSRF gate: IPv6/mapped/notation + IP pinning ------------------------------------------------\n201\tdef test_ssrf_gate_blocks_internal_including_ipv6():\n202\t    from sigil.agents.sources import is_public_host, read_source\n203\t    for internal in (\"127.0.0.1\", \"169.254.169.254\", \"10.0.0.1\", \"192.168.1.1\", \"localhost\",\n204\t                     \"::1\", \"fc00::1\", \"fe80::1\", \"::ffff:127.0.0.1\", \"0.0.0.0\"):\n205\t        assert is_public_host(internal) is False, f\"{internal} must be refused\"\n206\t    assert is_public_host(\"8.8.8.8\") is True\n207\t    assert read_source(\"http://127.0.0.1:9/secret\") == \"\", \"a loopback URL is refused before any request\"\n208\t    p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=\".txt\")\n209\t    Path(p).write_text(\"hello world\")\n210\t    assert \"hello\" in read_source(p), \"a local file still reads\"\n211\t\n212\t\n213\tdef test_ssrf_pins_the_vetted_ip_not_a_reresolve():\n214\t    import sigil.agents.sources as src\n215\t    calls = []\n216\t    orig_cc = src.socket.create_connection\n217\t    orig_vet = src._vetted_ip\n218\t    src._vetted_ip = lambda host: \"203.0.113.9\"      # gate sees a public IP\n219\t\n220\t    def spy(addr, *a, **k):\n221\t        calls.append(addr)\n222\t        raise OSError(\"blocked in test\")             # don't actually connect out\n223\t\n224\t    src.socket.create_connection = spy\n225\t    try:\n226\t        assert src.read_source(\"http://rebind.example/x\") == \"\"\n227\t    finally:\n228\t        src.socket.create_connection = orig_cc\n229\t        src._vetted_ip = orig_vet\n230\t    assert calls and calls[0][0] == \"203.0.113.9\", \"the socket is pinned to the vetted IP, not re-resolved\"\n231\t\n232\t\n233\t# ---- doctrine + integrity ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n234\tdef test_governance_imports_are_offense_free():\n235\t    import sigil.audit  # Two enforcement layers so a gesture can NEVER trigger an unintended action:\n3\t\n4\t  Layer 1 — the SESSION: `arm()` REQUIRES the owner key (it cannot be armed without the owner\n5\t  identity) and appends a signed `gesture.session_armed` record — the tamper-evident AUDIT proof-of-\n6\t  authorization, indicator-lit. The INJECTION gate itself is the live in-memory session, held ONLY by\n7\t  the owner's own running daemon process; it is BOUNDED by a TTL and ended by disarm / hand-loss /\n8\t  expiry. Injection is REFUSED with no live session.\n9\t\n10\t  Layer 2 — per intent, the tier is DERIVED from the WARDEN oracle (`hid.*` names): A1 (pointer\n11\t  move/click/scroll/drag) injects within the session; A2 (type/combo/app.launch) is QUEUED for a\n12\t  verified owner/device approval bound to `sha256(session_id|tool|args)` and NEVER auto-injected — so\n13\t  a gesture alone can never type a password or launch an app.\n14\t\n15\tOnly arm/disarm + DISCRETE actions (click/scroll/drag injected; type/launch queued) hit the spine —\n16\tper-frame pointer MOVES are telemetry (30 FPS records would DoS the append-only log).\"\"\"\n17\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n18\t\n19\timport math\n20\timport time\n21\timport uuid\n22\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n23\tfrom typing import Optional\n24\t\n25\t_KS_MIN_RESCAN = 0.05  # re-scan the kill-switch at most ~20x/s even on a churning spine (a cost floor)\n26\t\n27\tfrom ..agents.base import Tier\n28\tfrom ..reuse import sha256_hex\n29\tfrom .components import InputBackend\n30\tfrom .types import GestureIntent\n31\t\n32\tSESSION_ARMED = \"gesture.session_armed\"\n33\tSESSION_DISARMED = \"gesture.session_disarmed\"\n34\tACTION_SIGNAL = \"gesture.action\"\n35\tARM_REQUEST = \"gesture.arm_request\"\n36\t\n37\tMAX_DEVICE_TTL = 300.0        # a DEVICE-armed session is deliberately SHORTER than a local owner arm (1800)\n38\tARM_FRESHNESS = 30.0          # a device arm request must be recent (anti-stale / bounds the replay window)\n39\t_ARM_CORE = (\"signal\", \"device_id\", \"nonce\", \"ts\", \"ttl_seconds\")\n40\t\n41\tINTENT_TOOL = {\n42\t    \"move\": \"hid.pointer.move\", \"click\": \"hid.pointer.click\",\n43\t    \"scroll_left\": \"hid.pointer.scroll\", \"scroll_right\": \"hid.pointer.scroll\",\n44\t    \"drag\": \"hid.pointer.drag\", \"type\": \"hid.type\", \"combo\": \"hid.combo\", \"launch\": \"hid.app.launch\",\n45\t}\n46\t\n47\t\n48\tdef pending_device_arms(store, trusted_pubkey=None):\n49\t    \"\"\"ALL RECORDED device arm requests (written by the bridge's `submit_arm_request`) that have NOT yet\n50\t    armed a session, OLDEST-FIRST — candidates for `arm_by_device`, which RE-VERIFIES each fully (auth /\n51\t    freshness / kill-switch / replay / single-session / TTL). Returns a list (possibly empty). Oldest-first\n52\t    + returning ALL candidates means a newer STALE request never shadows an older still-valid one. This is\n53\t    the wiring that makes the remote-arm path reachable end-to-end (the gesture daemon consumes it).\"\"\"\n54\t    armed = set()\n55\t    cands = []\n56\t    for r in store.iter_records():\n57\t        p = r.payload\n58\t        if p.get(\"signal\") == SESSION_ARMED and p.get(\"armed_by\") == \"device\":\n59\t            armed.add((p.get(\"device_pubkey\"), p.get(\"nonce\")))\n60\t        elif (p.get(\"signal\") == ARM_REQUEST and p.get(\"decision\") == \"auto\"\n61\t              and p.get(\"sig\") and p.get(\"pubkey\")):\n62\t            cands.append(dict(p))\n63\t    return [c for c in cands if (c.get(\"pubkey\"), c.get(\"nonce\")) not in armed]\n64\t\n65\t\n66\tdef arm_request_message(core: dict) -> bytes:\n67\t    \"\"\"The canonical bytes a device signs to request an arm — ONLY the signed core fields, so a caller\n68\t    cannot smuggle unsigned extras. It composes the kill switch, budgets, and promotion policy into one fail-closed verdict:\n3\tAUTO (write it), QUEUE (hold for human approval), or DENY (refuse + log). The order matters and is\n4\tdeliberately conservative: observe is always allowed; a kill halts everything above observe; budget\n5\tis checked before any auto-grant; A2 auto-approves only under an explicit promotion; A3 never autos.\n6\t\n7\tKill/promotion are read FRESH per decision (a mid-run kill halts the rest of the run). Backward\n8\tcompatible: with no kill, no cap, and no promotion, A0/A1≤ceiling → AUTO and A2/A3 → QUEUE, exactly\n9\tas the pre-Phase-6 gate behaved.\"\"\"\n10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n11\t\n12\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n13\tfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\n14\tfrom enum import Enum\n15\tfrom typing import Optional\n16\t\n17\tfrom .budget import BudgetCaps, BudgetLedger\n18\tfrom .killswitch import KillSwitch\n19\tfrom .promotion import PromotionPolicy\n20\t\n21\t\n22\tclass Outcome(Enum):\n23\t    AUTO = \"auto\"\n24\t    QUEUE = \"queue\"\n25\t    DENY = \"deny\"\n26\t\n27\t\n28\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n29\tclass Decision:\n30\t    outcome: Outcome\n31\t    reason: str\n32\t\n33\t\n34\tdef _utc_day() -> str:\n35\t    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat()   # runtime bucketing only (never digested)\n36\t\n37\t\n38\tdef _load_caps() -> BudgetCaps:\n39\t    \"\"\"Optional per-agent caps from ~/.sigil/budgets.json ({daily_actions, daily_interrupts}).\n40\t    Absent/malformed → uncapped (budgets opt-in; default behavior unchanged).\"\"\"\n41\t    try:\n42\t        import json\n43\t\n44\t        from ..config import SIGIL_HOME\n45\t        f = SIGIL_HOME / \"budgets.json\"\n46\t        if not f.exists():\n47\t            return BudgetCaps()\n48\t        d = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n49\t        return BudgetCaps(daily_actions=d.get(\"daily_actions\"), daily_interrupts=d.get(\"daily_interrupts\"))\n50\t    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):\n51\t        return BudgetCaps()\n52\t\n53\t\n54\tclass Governor:\n55\t    def __init__(self, store, *, caps: Optional[BudgetCaps] = None, day_iso: Optional[str] = None,\n56\t                 owner_key=None, trusted_pubkey: Optional[str] = None):\n57\t        from .identity import owner_keypair, owner_pubkey\n58\t        self.store = store\n59\t        ok = owner_key if owner_key is not None else owner_keypair()\n60\t        tp = trusted_pubkey if trusted_pubkey is not None else owner_pubkey()\n61\t        self.kill = KillSwitch(store, owner_key=ok, trusted_pubkey=tp)\n62\t        self.promo = PromotionPolicy(store, owner_key=ok, trusted_pubkey=tp)\n63\t        self.budget = BudgetLedger(store, caps if caps is not None else _load_caps())\n64\t        self._day = day_iso\n65\t\n66\t    def decide(self, *, agent: str, tier, ceiling, scope: Optional[str] = None) -> Decision:\n67\t        from ..agents.base import AUTO_BAR, Tier\n68\t        scope = scope or \"*\"\n69\t\n70\t        # A0 observe/read is ALWAYS allowed — even under a kill switch (perception + memory stay alive).\n71\t        if tier <= Tier.A0:\n72\t            return Decision(Outcome.AUTO, \"observe (A0)\")\n73\t\n74\t        # KILL SWITCH: the mesh is halted; nothing above observe may act.\n75\t        if self.kill.is_engaged():\n76\t            return Decision(Outcome.DENY, \"kill switch engaged — agent mesh halted (A0 observe only)\")\n77\t\n78\t        # BUDGET: fail-closed — at cap, deny.\n79\t        over, why = self.budget.over_budget(agent, self._day or _utc_day())\n80\t        if over:\n81\t            return Decision(Outcome.DENY, why)\n82\t\n83\t        # Within the auto bar (A0/A1) and the agent's ceiling → auto, as always.\n84\t        if tier <= AUTO_BAR and tier <= ceiling:\n85\t            return Decision(Outcome.AUTO, f\"within auto bar ({tier.label()})\")\n86\t\n87\t        # A2 may auto-approve ONLY under an explicit per-scope promotion (never for ENVOY).\n88\t        if tier == Tier.A2 and tier <= ceiling and self.promo.is_promoted(agent, scope):\n89\t            return Decision(Outcome.AUTO, f\"A2 auto-approved by promotion ({agent}/{scope})\")\n90\t\n91\t        # Everything else (A2 unpromoted, A3, or above ceiling) queues for explicit human approval.\n92\t        return Decision(Outcome.QUEUE, f\"queued for approval ({tier.label()})\")\n93\t"}]},"uuid":"ab7a2a1e-2125-4ba9-ba3a-30df0a529be0","timestamp":"2026-07-19T09:18:37.639Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"9611d4c7-d82c-4140-9df1-67159e22defc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

The trust anchor is the SAME solo-owner\n2\tEd25519 keypair the spine checkpoint already persists (`KEYS_DIR/owner.priv|pub`, the 1-of-1 trust\n3\troot) — governance events (promotion grants, kill release, approvals) are signed by it and verified\n4\tagainst it. Reads are fail-closed: a missing key returns None, so nothing forged is ever trusted.\n5\t\n6\t`owner_pubkey()`/`owner_keypair()` READ the anchor (never generate — verification must not mint\n7\ttrust). `ensure_owner_keypair()` is for owner-initiated SIGNING actions (CLI engage/grant/approve):\n8\tit generates+persists the anchor once if absent, mirroring the checkpoint's `_owner_keys()`.\"\"\"\n9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n10\t\n11\timport os\n12\tfrom typing import Optional\n13\t\n14\tfrom ..config import KEYS_DIR\n15\tfrom ..reuse import KeyPair, generate_keypair\n16\t\n17\t_PRIV = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.priv\"\n18\t_PUB = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.pub\"\n19\t\n20\t\n21\tdef owner_pubkey() -> Optional[str]:\n22\t    try:\n23\t        return (_PUB.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip() or None)\n24\t    except OSError:\n25\t        return None\n26\t\n27\t\n28\tdef owner_keypair() -> Optional[KeyPair]:\n29\t    try:\n30\t        priv = _PRIV.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip()\n31\t        pub = _PUB.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip()\n32\t    except OSError:\n33\t        return None\n34\t    return KeyPair(public_key_b64=pub, private_key_b64=priv) if priv and pub else None\n35\t\n36\t\n37\tdef ensure_owner_keypair() -> KeyPair:\n38\t    \"\"\"Return the persisted owner keypair, generating+persisting it once if absent (owner signing\n39\t    path only). Same key material the checkpoint uses, so governance and the spine head share one\n40\t    owner identity.\"\"\"\n41\t    kp = owner_keypair()\n42\t    if kp is not None:\n43\t        return kp\n44\t    KEYS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n45\t    kp = generate_keypair()\n46\t    _PRIV.write_text(kp.private_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n47\t    _PUB.write_text(kp.public_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n48\t    for f in (_PRIV,):\n49\t        try:\n50\t            os.chmod(f, 0o600)\n51\t        except OSError:\n52\t            pass\n53\t    return kp\n54\t"}]},"uuid":"205a6cb9-1a02-4ee1-9eb2-29ed0a3a249a","timestamp":"2026-07-19T09:18:38.094Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"9ac9f03e-cef5-43d0-b0b3-5b248c310b47","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

Every state-changing governance event\n2\t(promotion grant/revoke, kill engage/release, approval approve/deny) carries an Ed25519 signature by\n3\tthe OWNER key over its canonical authenticated CORE fields, plus the signer's pubkey. Verification is\n4\tfail-closed: no trusted key, no signature, a pubkey that isn't the trusted owner key, or a tampered\n5\tcore → NOT authentic. This is the primitive that makes \"zero unauthorized A2/A3\" provable from the\n6\tlog rather than promised (a forged governance event never verifies, so it is ignored).\"\"\"\n7\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n8\t\n9\tfrom typing import Optional, Sequence\n10\t\n11\tfrom ..reuse import canonical_json, sign, verify_one\n12\t\n13\t\n14\tdef _canon(core: dict) -> bytes:\n15\t    m = canonical_json(core)\n16\t    return m if isinstance(m, bytes) else m.encode()\n17\t\n18\t\n19\tdef signed_payload(core: dict, owner_key) -> dict:\n20\t    \"\"\"core = the authenticated fields (must be JSON-canonicalizable). Returns core + {sig, pubkey}.\n21\t    With no owner key, sig/pubkey are None → the event will never verify (a caller that requires\n22\t    authentication must reject it).\"\"\"\n23\t    sig = sign(owner_key.private_key_b64, _canon(core)) if owner_key else None\n24\t    return {**core, \"sig\": sig, \"pubkey\": owner_key.public_key_b64 if owner_key else None}\n25\t\n26\t\n27\tdef verify_signed(payload: dict, core_fields: Sequence[str], trusted_pubkey: Optional[str]) -> bool:\n28\t    \"\"\"True iff `payload` carries a valid owner signature over its declared core fields. Fail-closed.\"\"\"\n29\t    if not trusted_pubkey:\n30\t        return False\n31\t    sig = payload.get(\"sig\")\n32\t    if not sig or payload.get(\"pubkey\") != trusted_pubkey:\n33\t        return False\n34\t    core = {k: payload.get(k) for k in core_fields}\n35\t    return verify_one(trusted_pubkey, _canon(core), sig)\n36\t"}]},"uuid":"957538dd-22ca-4005-a388-f9f547812690","timestamp":"2026-07-19T09:18:38.114Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"3412b81e-2650-4ee9-8a6e-44c7d470d0e9","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

no framework.* module may be loaded","new_string":"# ---- FIX 1: the seq -> byte-offset index is byte-identical to a full scan ------------------------\ndef test_offset_index_matches_full_scan():\n    \"\"\"get / iter_records(since_seq) / tail via the index return IDENTICAL records to a from-scratch\n    full scan — across random spine sizes, unicode payloads (byte != char offsets), and edge seqs.\n    Checked on BOTH a fresh store (index built lazily) and the append-maintained store.\"\"\"\n    rnd = random.Random(20260719)\n    for _ in range(15):\n        n = rnd.choice([1, 2, 3, 8, 25, 60])\n        p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=\".jsonl\")\n        s = SpineStore(p)\n        for i in range(n):\n            body = rnd.choice([\"e\", \"café ☕\", \"日本語テキスト\", \"x\"]) + f\"-{i}-{rnd.randint(0, 1_000_000)}\"\n            s.append(kind=\"message\", source=\"t\", actor=\"u\", payload={\"text\": body, \"i\": i})\n        truth = _full_scan(p)\n        assert [r.seq for r in truth] == list(range(n)), \"contiguous seqs from 0\"\n        for store in (SpineStore(p), s):                       # fresh (lazy build) AND append-maintained\n            for seq in range(-2, n + 2):                       # every seq + out-of-range edges\n                want = truth[seq] if 0 <= seq < n else None\n                assert store.get(seq) == want, f\"get({seq}) != scan (n={n})\"\n            for since in range(-2, n + 1):                     # every since_seq boundary\n                got = list(store.iter_records(since_seq=since))\n                exp = [r for r in truth if r.seq > since]\n                assert got == exp, f\"iter_records(since={since}) != scan (n={n})\"\n            for k in (0, 1, 3, n, n + 5):                      # tail windows incl. > len\n                got = [r.seq for r in store.tail(k)]\n                exp = [] if k <= 0 else [r.seq for r in truth][-k:]\n                assert got == exp, f\"tail({k}) != scan (n={n})\"\n\n\ndef test_index_extends_when_another_process_appends():\n    \"\"\"An append via a SECOND store instance (simulating another PROCESS) grows the file; a read on the\n    FIRST instance (whose index was already built) must detect the growth and return the new records.\"\"\"\n    p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=\".jsonl\")\n    a = SpineStore(p)\n    for i in range(4):\n        a.append(kind=\"message\", source=\"t\", actor=\"u\", payload={\"text\": f\"a{i}\"})\n    assert a.get(0).seq == 0, \"build the index on instance A\"                      # index now built\n    b = SpineStore(p)                                                              # \"another process\"\n    b.append(kind=\"message\", source=\"t\", actor=\"u\", payload={\"text\": \"from-B\"})    # seq 4, A doesn't know\n    assert a.get(4) is not None and a.get(4).text() == \"from-B\", \"A extends its index over B's append\"\n    assert [r.seq for r in a.iter_records(since_seq=2)] == [3, 4], \"A's index-seek sees B's record too\"\n\n\n# ---- FIX 2: torn-line tolerance (reads survive a torn tail; middle corruption fails verify) -------\ndef test_torn_last_line_is_tolerated_by_reads():\n    p, _ = _fresh(5)                                    # clean seq 0..4\n    with open(p, \"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n        f.write('{\"seq\": 5, \"scope\": \"sigil\", \"kind\": \"messa')   # a torn/partial LAST line, NO newline\n    s = SpineStore(p)                                   # __init__ must NOT crash (daemon can restart)\n    assert s.next_seq == 5, \"the tip is the last VALID record; the torn tail is skipped\"\n    assert [r.seq for r in s.iter_records()] == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4], \"reads skip the torn tail, no crash\"\n    assert s.get(4).seq == 4 and s.get(2).seq == 2, \"targeted reads survive the torn tail\"\n    assert [r.seq for r in s.tail(3)] == [2, 3, 4], \"tail survives the torn tail\"\n    ok, _ = s.verify()\n    assert ok, \"the valid prefix still verifies (a torn tail is a crash artifact, not tampering)\"\n\n\ndef test_torn_middle_line_still_fails_verify():\n    p, _ = _fresh(6)                                    # clean seq 0..5\n    lines = open(p).read().splitlines()\n    lines[2] = '{\"seq\": 2, \"kind\": \"messa'              # corrupt a MIDDLE line (real corruption/tamper)\n    open(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(lines) + \"\\n\")\n    s = SpineStore(p)\n    assert [r.seq for r in s.iter_records()] == [0, 1, 3, 4, 5], \"the corrupt middle line is skipped (a gap)\"\n    ok, msg = s.verify()\n    assert not ok and \"chain break\" in msg, f\"mid-file corruption must NEVER be hidden — verify() fails: {msg}\"\n\n\n# ---- FIX 3: fsync'd append stays chain-valid + durable across a reopen ----------------------------\ndef test_append_is_chain_valid_after_fsync():\n    p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=\".jsonl\")\n    s = SpineStore(p)\n    seqs = [s.append(kind=\"message\", source=\"t\", actor=\"u\", payload={\"text\": f\"e{i}\"}) for i in range(20)]\n    assert seqs == list(range(20)), \"the fsync'd appends produce a contiguous chain\"\n    ok, msg = s.verify()\n    assert ok, f\"the chain verifies after fsync appends: {msg}\"\n    s2 = SpineStore(p)                                  # reopen: the durable tip is read back\n    assert s2.next_seq == 20\n    assert s2.append(kind=\"message\", source=\"t\", actor=\"u\", payload={\"text\": \"more\"}) == 20\n    assert s2.verify()[0], \"the chain continues cleanly after a reopen\"\n\n\n# ---- FIX 4: the kill-switch state cache is correct AND invalidates on growth ----------------------\ndef test_killswitch_cache_correct_and_invalidates_on_growth():\n    from sigil.governor import KillSwitch\n    owner = reuse.generate_keypair()\n    pub = owner.public_key_b64\n    p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=\".jsonl\")\n    s = SpineStore(p)\n    s.append(kind=\"message\", source=\"t\", actor=\"u\", payload={\"text\": \"seed\"})\n    ks = KillSwitch(s, owner_key=owner, trusted_pubkey=pub)\n    assert ks.is_engaged() is False, \"no kill record → released\"\n    KillSwitch(s, owner_key=owner, trusted_pubkey=pub).engage(reason=\"drill\")     # append → file grows\n    assert ks.is_engaged() is True, \"an appended engage is honored on the next call (growth invalidates)\"\n    assert ks.is_engaged() is True, \"a repeat with no new append is a cache HIT with the same verdict\"\n    s.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"governor\", actor=\"WARDEN\",                     # forged UNSIGNED release\n             payload={\"signal\": \"governor.killswitch\", \"state\": \"released\"})\n    assert ks.is_engaged() is True, \"an unsigned release cannot revive the mesh — even through the cache\"\n    KillSwitch(s, owner_key=owner, trusted_pubkey=pub).release()                   # owner-signed → grows\n    assert ks.is_engaged() is False, \"an owner-signed release un-halts on the next call\"\n    # prove the cache is actually consulted: with no new appends the authoritative scan is NOT re-run\n    calls = {\"n\": 0}\n    real = ks._scan_engaged\n    ks._scan_engaged = lambda: (calls.__setitem__(\"n\", calls[\"n\"] + 1), real())[1]\n    assert ks.is_engaged() is False and ks.is_engaged() is False\n    assert calls[\"n\"] == 0, \"repeated calls with no new appends serve from cache without re-scanning (O(1))\"\n\n\ndef test_no_offense():\n    reuse.assert_no_offense()  # no framework.* module may be loaded"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":10775,"cache_read_input_tokens":142248,"output_tokens":2987,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":10775},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2987,"cache_read_input_tokens":142248,"cache_creation_input_tokens":10775,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":10775,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CdBBLkov2zn63aev5Abk7","attributionAgent":"general-purpose","type":"assistant","uuid":"79e5cd7b-af52-4585-a6c4-bb65969ab361","timestamp":"2026-07-19T09:28:36.639Z","effort":"xhigh","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

All four CRITICAL/HIGH audit findings fixed as transparent optimizations — the hash chain, cert digests, signed head, and public API behavior are byte-identical for clean spines. Tests: **integrity 18/18** (+6 new), **shared_primitives 14/14** (+1 new), **hardening 17/17** (unchanged — all still pass).\n\n### Changes per file\n\n**`sigil/spine/store.py`** (FIX 1, 2, 3-append)\n- Added module logger + `_REQUIRED_KEYS` (the fields `SpineRecord.from_dict` needs).\n- `__init__`: added the in-memory index state — `_index_lock` (threading.Lock), `_index_built`, `_offsets: dict[seq,int]`, `_max_seq`, `_scan_pos`.\n- `append`: capture `offset = os.fstat(f.fileno()).st_size` (byte offset where the line lands), then **`os.fsync(f.fileno())`** after `flush()` inside the lock/flock (FIX 3 — durable ack). Then O(1) index maintenance: only when `_index_built and _scan_pos == offset` (index exactly current), record `_offsets[seq]=offset` and advance `_scan_pos`. If another process appended in between (`_scan_pos < offset`), it skips and the next read re-extends — so a cross-process gap can never poison the index.\n- `iter_records`: now seeks to `_start_offset_for(since_seq)` and reads forward in **binary** mode. For `since_seq >= 0` it jumps straight to the line of `seq = since_seq+1` (O(records-returned)); for `since_seq < 0` it starts at byte 0 exactly as before. Malformed lines are skipped + warned, not raised (FIX 2).\n- `get`: O(1) via `_offsets[seq]` seek+readline; falls back to an index-seeked `iter_records` when a seq isn't indexed (beyond tip, or a corrupt line was skipped).\n- `_last_nonempty_line` (FIX 2): rewritten to skip a torn/garbage tail and return the last line that JSON-parses with the chain fields — a clean file returns the same last line byte-for-byte; a torn tail no longer crashes `__init__`/`append`, so the daemon restarts.\n- Added `_start_offset_for`, `_ensure_index` (lazy build; extend-on-growth via `stat().st_size` for cross-process appends; rebuild-on-shrink), `_scan_from` (indexes only newline-terminated lines; a trailing partial line is left for the next extend). `tail` left as-is (its seek-from-end is already bounded + torn-tolerant).\n\n**`sigil/spine/checkpoint.py`** (FIX 3-head): added `_atomic_write_text` (temp file in same dir → fsync → `os.replace()` → fsync dir; unlinks temp on failure). `checkpoint()` now writes the signed head through it, so a crash never leaves a torn/partial head. (`verify.py` needed no change — it only reads the head; the head is written only here.)\n\n**`sigil/governor/killswitch.py`** (FIX 4): `is_engaged()` now consults a module-level `_STATE_CACHE` keyed by `(resolved spine path, trusted_pubkey)` holding `(last-seen size, engaged)`. On each call it `stat`s the file — unchanged size ⇒ return the cached verdict O(1); grown/first-seen/shrunk ⇒ run the real scan (`_scan_engaged`, the old body verbatim — semantics untouched, owner-signed release still authoritative) and refresh. Append-only ⇒ any engage/release grows the file ⇒ the cache invalidates and the new state is honored next call. Keying on `trusted_pubkey` (beyond the spec's path-only) prevents instances with different trust roots from sharing a verdict.\n\n### Index design & byte-identical rationale\nAppend-only JSONL with contiguous seqs from 0 ⇒ offsets never move, so the index is a pure `seq→line-start-offset` map, only ever appended to. Full scans (`verify`/`count`/`entries`/`iter_records(-1)`) deliberately **bypass** the index (`_start_offset_for` returns 0 for `since_seq<0`), so they stay a single pass identical to the original. Targeted reads build the index once (the unavoidable scan) then are O(1)/O(returned). Byte-offsets are computed and consumed in binary throughout (verified against unicode payloads where byte≠char offsets). `json.loads(bytes)` and `SpineRecord.from_dict` yield records identical to the old text-mode path. The only behavioral change on any path is that a malformed line is now skipped+warned instead of raising — and a skipped MIDDLE line becomes a seq gap that `verify()` still fails on (proven by test), so mid-file tampering is never hidden.\n\n### New tests\n- `test_integrity.py`: `test_offset_index_matches_full_scan` (get/iter_records(since)/tail vs a from-scratch scan across 15 random spines, unicode bodies, every edge seq, on both fresh + append-maintained stores); `test_index_extends_when_another_process_appends`; `test_torn_last_line_is_tolerated_by_reads` (no crash, valid prefix verifies); `test_torn_middle_line_still_fails_verify` (skipped → gap → `verify()` fails with \"chain break\"); `test_append_is_chain_valid_after_fsync` (+ reopen continuation); `test_killswitch_cache_correct_and_invalidates_on_growth` (engage/forged-unsigned-release/signed-release transitions + proves repeated no-append calls don't re-scan).\n- `test_shared_primitives.py`: `test_iter_records_index_seek_matches_full_scan` (the exact index-seek path `SpineTailer.poll` relies on, across every cursor + a live poll over an append).\n\n### Known limitation (honest)\nFIX 2 guarantees reads/restart survive a torn tail; it does **not** repair it. If a legacy torn tail (no trailing newline) exists, a subsequent `append` writes contiguously after those bytes, merging them into one unparseable line — that record is then skipped by reads. FIX 3's fsync prevents torn writes from occurring in the first place, and I deliberately did **not** add tail-repair to `append` because it would change what's written to disk (against the invariant). FIX 4's cache yields O(1) for read-heavy consultation (the 30fps gesture loop, dashboard/CLI status, and cross-caller sharing on one path); a batch where every proposal auto-appends still re-scans per append, since each append is a real state change — this matches the spec's stated design.\n\nEverything left uncommitted."}],"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2279,"cache_read_input_tokens":164701,"output_tokens":3735,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":2279},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":3735,"cache_read_input_tokens":164701,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2279,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":2279,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CdBBeXVy6Yx5Vr5t52zSz","attributionAgent":"general-purpose","type":"assistant","uuid":"072ddcfc-7cc5-4931-b8dd-e01a5eddbee6","timestamp":"2026-07-19T09:32:54.353Z","effort":"xhigh","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}
